item.title: nuSTORM: a unique GeV electron-(anti)neutrino machine
item.description: arXiv:2611.27549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this conference contribution, I briefly review current experimental programmes measuring the Dirac CP phase {\delta}CP using accelerator neutrinos. I argue that the nuSTORM concept---neutrino beams from a muon storage ring---could provide high-quality electron-(anti)neutrino beams needed for the cross-section inputs to {\delta}CP measurements.
item.dc:creator: Xianguo Lu

item.title: Heat cleaning kinetics and thermal degradation of MOCVD-grown GaAs photocathodes
item.description: arXiv:2611.27833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluated metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaAs/GaAsP strained-superlattice photocathodes with integrated distributed Bragg reflectors in a low-voltage Mott polarimeter at Jefferson Lab. Without a protective arsenic cap, surface contamination can develop during transport and installation. Heat cleaning removes this contamination by thermally desorbing material bound to the surface, but excessive heating can also damage the photocathode. We modeled quantum efficiency (QE) in terms of surface contaminant coverage to describe its increase with heating time. QE rose more rapidly and reached a plateau nearly twice as high at $550^\circ\text{C}$ as at $450^\circ\text{C}$, while polarization remained near 83%. Further heating reduced QE and polarization. Reflectance measurements showed a shift of the optical resonance to shorter wavelengths, consistent with surface material loss. We also tested the cleaning method in a high-voltage photogun, where QE showed the same initial increase and subsequent decline. The cleaning procedure must therefore balance contaminant removal against loss of photocathode material.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Blume, Adam Masters, Colin Kirk, Sushil Poudel, John Hill, Alimohammed Kachwala, Joseph Grames, Marcy L Stutzman, Sylvain Marsillac, Matt Grau

item.title: Feasibility study of two-stage direct laser acceleration of electrons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the first numerical demonstration of two-stage direct laser acceleration (DLA) of electrons. The result was obtained using quasi-3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. The first stage ($a_0 = 6$, $\tau = 200~\mathrm{fs}$, $w = 4\lambda$, $\lambda = 0.8~\mu\mathrm{m}$) utilized a nitrogen gas target with an atomic density of $n_a = 0.008n_{cr}$. This stage was designed to accelerate low-energy electrons, achieving a maximum energy of approximately 94 MeV with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 7.0$ MeV and $T_2 = 16.0$ MeV) and a charge of 6.04 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The resulting electron bunch was then injected into the second stage, where hydrogen at a lower density ($n_a = 0.01n_{cr}$) was used, while the laser parameters were the same as in the first stage except that the waist was increased to $w = 8\lambda$. After the second stage, the electrons reached energies up to 225 MeV, with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 18.4$ MeV and $T_2 = 88.3$ MeV) and a charge of 4.55 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The self-injected electrons in the second stage reached a maximum energy of 123 MeV with a charge of 1.14 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The simulation results are compared with a theoretical DLA model, which describes the electron motion in the combined fields of the laser pulse and the quasistatic plasma channel. The model accounts for the transverse size of the channel by incorporating a Gaussian attenuation of the channel fields and off-axis injection. The theoretical model correctly describes the observed acceleration dynamics for both low-energy and pre-accelerated electrons, confirming its validity for designing multi-stage DLA schemes. Thus, the implementation of multi-stage acceleration by the DLA mechanism is successfully demonstrated for the first time in a numerical experiment.
item.dc:creator: E. Starodubtseva, S. Solntsev, I. Tsymbalov, A. Savel'ev

item.title: Single-Pulse Dosimetry for Ultra-High-Dose-Rate X-Ray Pulses Based on Radiation-Induced Acoustic Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.27772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time dosimetry of ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) pulsed X-rays remains a major challenge. This proof-of-principle study investigates a dosimetry method for UHDR pulsed X-rays based on radiation-induced acoustic (RA) signals from a thin metal foil. The foil combines efficient X-ray absorption and acoustic resonance, converting deposited dose into acoustic signals with discrete resonant frequencies. Single-pulse measurements were performed at six dose levels spanning approximately 1--40 mGy(Si), with one pulse recorded at each level and instantaneous dose rates reaching the order of 10^6 Gy/s at the highest dose settings. The peak-to-peak amplified transducer-output voltage exhibited a linear relationship with the reference dose measured by thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs). These results demonstrate the feasibility of single-pulse acoustic dosimetry under the tested conditions. Furthermore, we establish analytical solutions for radiation-induced acoustic signals in a one-dimensional layered medium in both the time and frequency domains, providing a theoretical basis for signal interpretation and detector optimization.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Han, Ke Chen, Chenghao Hua, Haoran Chen, Lili Ding, Changhui Li, Xiaoping Ouyang, Chenhui Wang, Wei Chen, Wenjun Ma

item.title: Continuous-Wave Operation at 30 MV/m of a Superconducting Radio-Frequency Gun Cryomodule with an Exchangeable Cathode Plug
item.description: arXiv:2609.12233v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

item.title: Experimental Evidence for MeV Undulator Radiation Generated by Ultrarelativistic Positrons in a Periodically Bent Crystal
item.description: arXiv:2611.15542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report evidence for undulator radiation generated by ultrarelativistic positrons in a large-amplitude, long-period crystalline undulator. A pattern of Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors periodically bend the (110) planes of a Silicon crystal with a geometry measured independently by x-ray diffraction. Under planar alignment, the forward energy loss showed a localized excess at $6.8 \pm 0.3$~MeV ($4.05\sigma$), matching the predictions of simulations. Experimental results also indicate that an intense positron beam could make the undulator competitive in brilliance with state-of-the-art inverse-Compton gamma-ray sources.
